Amplitude-VCMixer.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.2.5 binary. The gain knobs run minus 1 to plus 1 with a default of 0, and the amplifier output is simply the input times that number, so the module is silent as it arrives and the outputs carry whatever voltage is fed in rather than a fixed range. The strength CV multiplies the knob rather than adding to it, at a fifth per volt, and with the jack empty the multiplier is exactly 1. The accent envelope is applied only when the accent jack has a cable in it, and only to the first amplifier: AmplitudeVCMixer::process at 0x13154 chooses between the plain gain and the gain times one half of the envelope plus one, and the second amplifier's gain at 0x13158 has no such term. The accent length knob runs 0.1 to 1 with a default near 0.505 and is squared and multiplied by 15 before it reaches the envelope. The panel prints almost nothing: AMPLITUDE, STRENGTH twice, ACCENT and a summation sign, with the jacks marked by icons rather than words, so most lines here start with what the control does rather than with a label. Eight lamps are driven, four per amplifier, from the signs of the audio and the gain.

Juicy-VCF.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.2.5 binary. The frequency knob runs 0.08 to 0.99 with a default of 0.5 and is displayed as a percentage; resonance runs 0.00001 to 0.99 with a default of 0.0001, so the filter starts with essentially none. The unnamed knob runs 1 to 3, snapped, and the value is passed straight through as the model number to VcfModels::setParams. The filter is run four times oversampled. JuicyVCF::process does no work at all unless a cable is in the output: 0x16fe4 tests the output port's channel count before calling the filter, and 0x1709c does the same before setting the channel count. The two frequency CV jacks read voltages at the loop's channel index rather than through getPolyVoltage, so a one-channel cable in either of them reaches only the first voice. The accent envelope is advanced only while the accent jack is connected, and its last value is otherwise retained and still multiplies the cutoff. The panel prints JUICY, OTA SVF, FREQUENCY, RESONANCE, ACCENT, INPUT and, under the audio output jack, 24db; the two frequency CV jacks and three of the knobs carry no lettering at all.

Vector-Synth.notes: Closed source; read from the installed 2.2.5 binary, which is the Free cut of the maker's Detour. The panel is titled DETOUR and the module browser calls it Detour Free, while the model slug is Vector-Synth. Parameter ranges: PITCH 0 to 8.5834 with a default at 4.2917, V1 and V2 0 to 4 with a default of 0.5, D1 and D2 declared from 0.5 down to 0 with a default of 0, so those two knobs run backwards, FREQ 0.001 to 1 with a default of 1, RESO 0 to 0.99 with a default of 0.5, decay and sustain defaulting to 1 and attack and release to 0, and every attenuator and envelope amount 0 to 1 with a default of 0. The octave switch gives minus two, minus one and no offset for its three positions, and defaults to minus one. Six parameters, indices 6 to 11, are declared and given no widget and are read nowhere in process; they cannot be clicked and get no line. Four more, indices 26, 32, 33 and 34, are the SLOW R button and the three view buttons: they are never passed to configParam, so they carry Rack's default quantity with no name, but process reads all four and they each toggle a flag and light a lamp. The three view flags reach only Display::drawLayer, which uses them to choose between drawing the parameter, the attenuator, the envelope amount or the mix for the red pair, the blue pair and the filter. The V and D CV jacks, the FM jack and the filter CV jack are all read at channel one only; the pitch and gate jacks are read channel by channel. Five lamps show the voltage on the V, D and filter CV jacks at half scale. The context menu holds only Model 2 (softer sound and V modulation):  and High Quality, both saved in the patch along with the long envelope and linear FM flags.
